sources: The Complete Book of Ayurvedic Home Remedies - Vasant Lad.pdf
meta.scope_note: Wellness, daily routine (Dinacharya), stress pacing, and somatic resets only—not medical diagnosis or clinical treatment[cite: 1, 7].

vata.stress_signature: Restless thoughts, overstimulation, scattered focus, light or disrupted sleep[cite: 1, 7].
daily_reset: Keep regular wake, meal, and wind-down times (aiming to wind down by ~10 PM)[cite: 1].
Choose warm, grounding meals and warm drinks over cold, rushed, or overly caffeinated habits[cite: 1].
Practice slow, steady breathing and step away from noisy or fragmented screens[cite: 1].

pitta.stress_signature: Inner heat, sharp impatience, overwork, or reactive irritation when pushed too hard[cite: 1, 7].
daily_reset: Take cooling pauses, step outside for fresh air, and avoid over-scheduling back-to-back battles[cite: 1].
Favor cooling, soothing foods and calm hydration when feeling overheated or driven[cite: 1].
Use slow, cooling breathwork and deliberate unclenching before replying[cite: 1].

kapha.stress_signature: Mental heaviness, sluggishness, resistance to starting, or comfort-seeking inertia[cite: 1, 7].
daily_reset: Start the day with brisk movement or a walk rather than lingering in heavy inertia[cite: 1].
Keep mornings light and structured with small, clear first steps[cite: 1].
Use energizing, rhythmic breathwork to lift mental fog[cite: 1].

somatic_90_second_reset.step_1_body_anchor: Drop your shoulders, unclench your jaw, let your tongue rest lightly, and press both feet flat into the floor to feel solid ground[cite: 12].
somatic_90_second_reset.step_2_breath_pause: Take a few slow, unforced breaths and notice the brief, quiet pause at the end of the exhale without straining[cite: 12].
somatic_90_second_reset.step_3_witness_shift: Step back from the racing thought or feeling—observe it as passing weather rather than an urgent command to react[cite: 12].
